title: Cofinite topology and nonunique limits
section: Practice Test ▷ Question 58: a topology with finite complements
terms: cofinite topology; finite-complement topology; T1 separation; nonunique sequence limit.

exposition.text:
The cofinite topology on a set X consists of ∅ together with all subsets whose complements are
finite. Its closed sets are the finite sets and X itself. On a finite set it is discrete. On an infinite
set every two nonempty open sets intersect, so it is connected and is not Hausdorff; nevertheless
every singleton is closed, which is the T separation property.
1
Every subset is compact with its subspace topology: in a cover choose one nonempty member,
which leaves only finitely many points uncovered, and cover those points using finitely many
more members. A sequence converges to x precisely when it eventually avoids each finite subset
not containing x. Thus a sequence of distinct points converges to every point. These exam-
ples explain why compact subsets need not be closed without a Hausdorff hypothesis, and why
uniqueness of limits requires a separation assumption.

all but finitely many terms of the distinct sequence 1, 2, 3, . . .. Thus x → x for every real

An infinite set X has the cofinite topology. Which subsets of X are compact in their subspace
topology?
(A) Only finite subsets and X
(B) Only finite subsets
(C) Only X itself
(D) Only countable subsets
(E) Every subset

solution.text:
Every subset inherits the cofinite topology (which is discrete when the subset is finite).
In an open cover of a nonempty subset, one nonempty member leaves only finitely many
uncovered points, each covered by one further member. Thus a finite subcover always
exists.

question.text:
A continuous map from an infinite cofinite space to a Hausdorff space must have which prop-
erty?
(A) Its image is infinite.
(B) It is injective.
(C) It is surjective.
(D) Its image has exactly two points.
(E) It is constant.

solution.text:
Any two nonempty open subsets of an infinite cofinite space intersect. If the map took
two distinct values, disjoint Hausdorff neighborhoods of those values would have disjoint
nonempty open preimages, a contradiction. Hence the map is constant.
